Write SQL with a window function for iowa_sales.BottlesSold (share of total).

Keep it simple:
SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) AS sum_bottlessold,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) / SUM(SUM(s.BottlesSold)) OVER () AS share_of_total
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName
ORDER BY sum_bottlessold DESC;
What about ranking within category?

SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  i.ItemName,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) AS sum_bottlessold,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CategoryName ORDER BY SUM(s.BottlesSold) DESC) AS rnk_in_category
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
JOIN iowa_item i ON s.ItemID = i.ItemID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName, i.ItemName;
Is this necessary at the beginning?
No. This is advanced analytics. Start with GROUP BY + SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX.

SELECT x.VendorName AS by_vendorname,
       SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS sum_bottlevolumeml,
       AVG(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS avg_bottlevolumeml,
       MIN(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS min_bottlevolumeml,
       MAX(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS max_bottlevolumeml
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_vendor x ON s.VendorID = x.VendorID
GROUP BY x.VendorName
ORDER BY sum_bottlevolumeml DESC;
Jak ograniczyć do top 10?
Dodaj LIMIT 10 po ORDER BY.
A jak policzyć tylko liczbę wierszy?
Zamień miary na COUNT(*) albo COUNT(DISTINCT ...), zależnie od potrzeby.
Write SQL with a window function for iowa_sales.StateBottleCost (share of total).

Clear and direct:
SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  SUM(s.StateBottleCost) AS sum_statebottlecost,
  SUM(s.StateBottleCost) / SUM(SUM(s.StateBottleCost)) OVER () AS share_of_total
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName
ORDER BY sum_statebottlecost DESC;
What about ranking within category?

SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  i.ItemName,
  SUM(s.StateBottleCost) AS sum_statebottlecost,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CategoryName ORDER BY SUM(s.StateBottleCost) DESC) AS rnk_in_category
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
JOIN iowa_item i ON s.ItemID = i.ItemID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName, i.ItemName;
Is this necessary at the beginning?
No. This is advanced analytics. Start with GROUP BY + SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX.

SELECT x.CalendarMonth AS by_calendarmonth,
       SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS sum_bottlevolumeml,

Zamień miary na COUNT(*) albo COUNT(DISTINCT ...), zależnie od potrzeby.

Write SQL with a window function for iowa_sales.BottleVolumeMl (share of total).

Plainly:
SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS sum_bottlevolumeml,
  SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl) / SUM(SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl)) OVER () AS share_of_total
FROM iowa_sales s

ORDER BY sum_bottlevolumeml DESC;

  c.CategoryName,
  i.ItemName,
  SUM(s.BottleVolumeMl) AS sum_bottlevolumeml,

JOIN iowa_item i ON s.ItemID = i.ItemID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName, i.ItemName;

JOIN iowa_item i ON s.ItemID = i.ItemID

Clear and direct:
SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) AS sum_bottlessold,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) / SUM(SUM(s.BottlesSold)) OVER () AS share_of_total
FROM iowa_sales s

GROUP BY c.CategoryName
ORDER BY sum_bottlessold DESC;
What about ranking within category?

SELECT
  c.CategoryName,
  i.ItemName,
  SUM(s.BottlesSold) AS sum_bottlessold,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CategoryName ORDER BY SUM(s.BottlesSold) DESC) AS rnk_in_category
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
JOIN iowa_item i ON s.ItemID = i.ItemID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName, i.ItemName;
Is this necessary at the beginning?
No. This is advanced analytics. Start with GROUP BY + SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX.

Write SQL with multiple aggregations for iowa_sales.Pack.

Straight up:
SELECT
  SUM(Pack) AS sum_pack,
  AVG(Pack) AS avg_pack,
  MIN(Pack) AS min_pack,
  MAX(Pack) AS max_pack,
  COUNT(*)  AS cnt_rows
FROM iowa_sales;
How do I do it by category?

SELECT c.CategoryName,
  SUM(s.Pack) AS sum_pack,
  AVG(s.Pack) AS avg_pack,
  MIN(s.Pack) AS min_pack,
  MAX(s.Pack) AS max_pack
FROM iowa_sales s
JOIN iowa_category c ON s.CategoryID = c.CategoryID
GROUP BY c.CategoryName
ORDER BY sum_pack DESC;
